paragraphs.text: Recover a broken DeepSeek Harness profile: test-boot a copy, disable selected plugins, snapshots, an
d a local recovery UI.
# dsh-safe

An out-of-band safety net for DeepSeek Harness plugins, shipped as both a
command-line tool and an i

ety net for DeepSeek Harness plugins, shipped as both a
command-line tool and an installable bundle.

The problem: a plugin can stop the Harness from opening. Sometimes the process
crashes and the crash

dialog loops; sometimes the window hangs on "loading"
forever. The built-in recovery dialog ("Disab

le third-party plugins, back up the
profile patch and restart") fires only on a crash, and it is all

-or-nothing: it
removes *every* third-party bundle and detaches the whole patch layer. Usually you
o
nly want to switch off the one plugin you were working on.

`dsh-safe` runs from a terminal while the app is closed and edits the profile
files directly, so it

does not depend on the broken Harness booting at all. The
bundle adds two read-mostly tools to a hea

lthy session: inspect the profile and
boot evidence, and snapshot the profile before a change.
## Install
As a plugin, which adds the two in-harness tools:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Restart DeepSeek Harness. The plugin manager lists **dsh-safe**, and the model can
call `dsh_safe_st

atus` and `dsh_safe_snapshot`. The CLI files ship inside the same
package, so the recovery commands

_snapshot`. The CLI files ship inside the same
package, so the recovery commands below keep working.

As a standalone CLI, no install step is required: clone the repo, open a terminal
in `tools/dsh-safe

`, and run `dsh-safe.cmd` (or `node dsh-safe.mjs`). The only
dependency is Node.js 22+. The recovery

CLI targets Windows (it uses `tasklist`,
`cmd.exe` and the desktop executable); the in-harness tool

s are plain Node and
work wherever the Harness runs.

The plugin half is a convenience, not the recovery path: when the Harness cannot
boot, nothing insid

e it can run. Recovery always goes through the CLI or the
recovery page, from outside the app.
## In-harness tools
| Tool | What it does |
| `dsh_safe_status` | Active profile, selected bundles (and which are local links), recent snapshots
, last known-good snapshot, last test boot, last recovery, newest startup-failure log with the plugi

ns that failed or waited for services |
| `dsh_safe_snapshot` | Copies `package.json`, `cordis.yml`
and `cordis.patch.yml` into `$DSH_HOME/safety/snapshots/<id>/`; optional `label` and `note` |

Both tools call the same functions as the CLI, so a snapshot taken by the model is
the same snapshot

`dsh-safe snapshots` lists and `dsh-safe restore` accepts.
Neither tool changes the plugin selectio

n: disabling and restoring are done from
the CLI while the app is closed.
## Quick start

Before you change anything, or right before you try a risky plugin:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## The commands
| Command | What it does |
| `status` | Shows profile path, whether the app is running, bundle/local counts, recent plugin oper

ations, crash evidence |
| `snapshot [-l label]` | Copies `package.json` + `cordis.yml` + `cordis.pa

tch.yml` into a timestamped snapshot |
| `snapshots` / `list` | Lists snapshots (`--json` for script

ing) |
| `restore [id\|latest]` | Puts a snapshot back; the current state is saved as a new snapshot

first |
| `plugins` / `bundles` | Numbered list of selected bundles with a `[core/local/official/th

ird-party/installed]` tag |
| `disable [name...]` | Removes bundles from `dsh.profile.bundles`; no n

ames = interactive picker |
| `enable [name...]` | Adds installed bundles back; no names = interacti

ve picker |
| `try` | Clone this profile under a temporary name, boot it in an isolated `DSH_HOME`,

wait for the web server, probe it, then delete the clone |
| `ui` | Start a local recovery page: cra

sh evidence, plugin checkboxes, snapshots, "test boot", "launch" |
| `recover` | Reads the newest st

artup log and explains which plugin failed and why |
| `recover --pick --apply` | Shows suspect plug

ins, lets you pick which ones to disable, applies it |
| `recover --apply` | Disables the newest saf

e suspect |
| `recover --safe-mode --apply` | Keeps only `dsh-base` + `dsh-web-app` (profile still i

ntact) |
| `open` | Runs `try`; if the boot fails it auto-disables the mapped culprit, retries, and
only then launches the app |

`disable`/`enable` accept names or entry ids (`include:workflow-kit`), and
`--dry-run` prints the pl

an. Core bundles (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-base`,
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app`) are refused unless you pass `

--force` — disabling them
takes the whole app down.
## Recovery recipes

**1. The app crashes on launch (dialog says "Host process exited").**
Do not click the built-in "Dis

able third-party plugins" button unless you want to
lose every third-party bundle. Instead:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

**2. The app opens and hangs on "loading" forever.**
The built-in dialog never appears for a hang. R

un `dsh-safe.cmd recover` first: the
startup log usually names the plugin that threw during `apply()

`. Then
`dsh-safe.cmd recover --pick --apply`.

**3. You installed a plugin and now nothing works.**
`status` shows the newest `install/*` operation

, `plugins` shows the bundle list.
Disable the last thing you installed:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

**4. You want to test a profile change before letting it near the real app.**
`dsh-safe.cmd try` — s

ame bundles, same `node_modules` (via a junction), but a
throwaway profile name and `DSH_HOME`. The
real profile is only read.

**5. You disabled the wrong thing.**
`dsh-safe.cmd snapshots`, then `dsh-safe.cmd restore <id>`. `re

store` with no id
restores the newest snapshot; either way the current state is backed up first, so
restore is itself undoable.
## The recovery UI

`dsh-safe-ui.cmd` (or `dsh-safe.cmd ui`) starts a tiny web server on `127.0.0.1`
and opens it in you

r browser. It runs as a normal Node process, so it works while
the Harness is crashed, hung, or clos

rowser. It runs as a normal Node process, so it works while
the Harness is crashed, hung, or closed.
The page shows:

- **Last startup evidence** — the error line, the failed plugins with their first
exception, which p

lugins waited for services, and the suspect list. Each failed
